justification_text:
At the time of the forecast, gold was trading near the $1,840–$1,850 range, and my one-day point estimate of $1,848 essentially reflected a near-term continuation of that price level with minimal drift expected over a single session. Short-term gold price dynamics tend to be dominated by intraday momentum, dollar index movements, and Treasury yield fluctuations, none of which I had strong reason to expect would shift dramatically within 24 hours. The one-week estimate of $1,860 reflected a modest upward bias based on the general macro backdrop at the time — persistent uncertainty around Federal Reserve policy, moderate safe-haven demand, and a slightly softer dollar trend. The one-month estimate of $1,880 extended that same gentle bullish lean, incorporating the possibility of continued disinflation narratives that sometimes support gold by lowering real yields.

The confidence interval widths grow substantially across horizons for straightforward reasons. Over one day, gold typically moves within a band of roughly plus or minus 1–2%, giving a relatively tight interval. Over one week, scheduled economic data releases, Fed speaker commentary, and geopolitical developments introduce meaningful variance, widening the band to around plus or minus 6–7%. Over one month, the uncertainty compounds further — central bank decisions, shifts in inflation expectations, dollar trends, and global risk appetite can each independently move gold by several percent, justifying the roughly $230 wide interval at the one-month horizon.

Specific risks that could push outcomes outside those stated intervals are meaningful in both directions. On the upside, an unexpected deterioration in U.S. banking stress, a sharper-than-anticipated economic slowdown signaling a Fed pivot, or a geopolitical shock such as an escalation in a major conflict could send gold well above $2,100 within a month. On the downside, a surprisingly strong U.S. jobs report or inflation reading that re-accelerates Fed tightening expectations could push real yields sharply higher, potentially driving gold below $1,650 or even lower. Thin liquidity episodes, such as those around major central bank decisions or unexpected sovereign events, can also produce outsized moves that my interval widths may understate.
